Home / Services / Precious metals assaying
09 / ASSAYING

Measured composition begins with the right specimen.

Assaying is the examination or measurement of a material to answer defined questions about composition or content. For precious metals, the relationship between the material, the sampling plan and the analytical technique is central to interpreting the result.

THE SERVICE IN CONTEXT

A defined scope leads to a better decision.

Explore sampling, precious-metal content, method suitability and assay interpretation.

The suitable approach depends on the material, the intended outcome and the details agreed by the parties.

Make a service enquiry ↗
A CLOSER LOOK

What deserves attention.

Different specimen forms and questions call for different considerations. The following themes help frame the discussion.

01

Understanding what an assay measures

An assay may focus on the proportion of a precious metal, relevant accompanying constituents or characteristics required for a particular decision. Different sample forms call for different preparation and evaluation considerations.

02

Selecting methods for the actual question

Industry methods can include fire assay, X-ray fluorescence and instrumental chemical analysis. These are examples rather than a list of instruments operated by ASL; the appropriate technique depends on material, required analytes, sensitivity and agreed scope.

03

From test portion to useful result

A report needs to link each stated result to the particular specimen examined, its identity and measurement units. When results inform a larger lot, sampling representativeness and any technical limitations should also be considered.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

What to prepare.

A few useful details can make your first enquiry much more focused.

  • Precious-metal type or suspected composition
  • Material form and approximate mass
  • Known source and sampling method, if applicable
  • Existing results or supporting documents
  • Measurements or fineness questions to resolve
Explore preparation guides ↗
COMMON QUESTIONS

A little more clarity.

Can appearance alone establish fineness?+
No. A reliable assessment relies on appropriate evidence rather than colour or visual appearance.
Is an assay the same as a valuation?+
No. Composition is one possible input to valuation; market price and commercial settlement involve additional factors.
